variants.headline: Looking back: full shelves, empty household purses
variants.sub: Households are hungry despite available food because they do not have the money to buy it.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: Food was for sale, but households cannot afford it and were going hungry beside full shelves.

The shelves are full. The people beside them can still be hungry. That is not a contradiction; it is the problem. Readers deserve an answer to the question of what someone can afford, rather than a cheerful description of how much there is for somebody with the money to buy it.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The role of {target} warrants scrutiny through household purchasing power. This paper keeps affordability distinct from the availability of food, so that the practical question is not lost in a description of full shelves.
